blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: The harness plans an export three times, in fresh processes, and gets one digest three times. What does that show?

options.text: The plan is optimal with a zero gap, since three runs agreed on it
options.says: The runs stopped at HiGHS's 0.01% gap; agreeing runs say nothing about the gap.

options.text: This input, version and thread count give the same plan each run
options.says: Right: that is why the version and threads are in the manifest.

options.text: Any OR-Tools version will give this plan, since the input is fixed
options.says: Another version may differ; the manifest records the version for that reason.

options.text: The plan is the only best plan, since no run found another one
options.says: Equal digests do not show that no other plan ties on NPV.

origin.section: A Run Is Repeatable When Its Plan Digest Repeats

questions.stem: A change cuts each project's window one year short. Every rule test still passes. Which check reports the change?

options.text: The harness, since the faulty code gives a new digest on each run
options.says: The faulty code still repeats itself; the harness compares runs of the same code.

options.text: The deletion filter, since the faulty plan breaks one of the rows
options.says: The faulty plans keep every row the faulty code builds.

options.text: The manifest, since it records the window of each funded project
options.says: The manifest records hashes, the solver and the plan digest, not the windows.

options.text: The golden check, since a known plan's start no longer appears
options.says: Right: on the demo export P001's 2029 start vanished.

origin.section: A Golden Plan Catches a Regression the Rule Tests Miss

questions.stem: After a 2031 budget cut, last cycle's plan overspends 2031 and is handed to HiGHS as a hint. What did the medium run show?

options.text: The warm solve was faster, since it began from a nearly right plan
options.says: The warm run took the same 8,850 nodes as the cold one.

options.text: The warm solve was refused, since the hint breaks a budget row
options.says: The warm run finished OPTIMAL; a hint is a suggestion, not a row.

options.text: The warm solve did the same work as the cold one, to the node
options.says: Right: both runs took 8,850 nodes and 370,025 simplex iterations.

options.text: The warm solve found a better plan, since it searched from the old one
options.says: Both runs found the same NPV, $225,079.0k.

origin.section: A Warm Start Changed the Search, Not the Time, on These Runs

concepts: what a warm start did on the medium runs
